Gina — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. High level summary below; I can walk through details on a 30-minute call.

Short answer / recommended starting point:
- If your priority is strong isolation + least blast radius across accounts, start with PrivateLink (interface endpoints) per-region. It provides per-service endpoint controls and avoids wide cross-VPC routing changes.
- If you need very low-latency intra-VPC flow and have centralized networking control (single account or tightly managed peering), VPC Peering yields the simplest path and slightly lower latency.
- If you must reach on-prem infra broadly and want encryption across public Internet without private endpoints, S2S VPN is a good fallback; expect higher latency and more operational overhead.

I'll attach a short quick-comparison PDF and propose a small pilot plan (PrivateLink in primary region + S2S backfill for legacy on-prem).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick tech call this week to align on latency SLOs for typical inference payloads (tokens/sec and RTT targets).
2) We'll prepare an on-ramp checklist (endpoint subnets, NACLs, SG pins, MTLS, cert + rotation plan).
3) Draft SOW and timeline for pilot (2–3 weeks to a PrivateLink pilot).

Warmly,
Grace O'Connor

Quick technical summary for the brief (pasted back as bullets you can share):

VPC Peering
- Latency: Lowest RTT inside same region; no NAT traversal or extra hops. Expect ~1–5ms for intra-region peered VPCs for control-plane and data-plane flows (depends on AZ placement).
- Throughput: Unlimited in concept, bounded by instance/network ENI; good for high-throughput batch inference.
- Security: Route-based access, needs careful route table hygiene. Cross-account peering expands blast radius if misconfigured.
- Ops: Simple to set up; changes to CIDR or overlapping IPs require rework. No native endpoint-level IAM.
- When to use: Single-account or single-VPC per-customer deployments where you control both sides and want lowest latency.

PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints)
- Latency: Adds small hop (ENI + AWS-managed NLB); expect +3–10ms vs peering in same region depending on path and concurrency. Typically stable and predictable.
- Throughput: Good for RPC-style calls; per-endpoint bandwidth limits apply—scale with multiple endpoints/NLBs.
- Security: Endpoint-level controls and policy; supports VPC endpoint policies, private DNS, and strong least-privilege. Good for regulated customers.
- Ops: Requires endpoint provisioning per-region; easier to limit blast radius and audit access. Works well with cross-account service model.
- When to use: Multi-account SaaS where you want strict service boundaries and auditability.

Site-to-Site VPN
- Latency: Depends on public path and encryption; adds tens to low-hundreds ms if transcontinental or via congested links. For on-prem co-lo within same region, expect 10–40ms typical.
- Throughput: Limited by VPN appliance, session MTU, and public bandwidth. Not ideal for sustained high qps without additional optimization/banding.
- Security: Encrypted over public internet; combine with MTLS at application layer for defense-in-depth.
- Ops: Higher operational overhead (tunnel health, BGP, rekeying). Good fallback when direct cloud-native approaches aren't feasible.
- When to use: Legacy datacenters, constrained network teams, or when customer cannot accept cloud-native endpoints.

Operational considerations / monitoring hooks
- Observability: Instrument per-endpoint request latency, error rates, and token-level cost breakdown. Add synthetic probes from customer infra to the endpoint.
- Security & audit: Ship flow logs, endpoint access logs, and TLS cert rotation events to a central audit bucket. KMS integration for secrets & key ops.
- Fallback strategy: Canary PrivateLink in primary region, fallback route via S2S for on-prem; use routing policies to fail-open to a lower-capacity path.

Final one-line recommendation:
- For EdgeBank: Start with PrivateLink per primary region for strict control + auditability; add an S2S VPN stitching only for on-prem regions that cannot use PrivateLink, and reserve VPC peering for narrow low-latency intra-cloud pilots where we control both VPCs.

Gina — team has reviewed and we recommend the following pragmatic onboarding path for EdgeBank. Ive kept the action items and timeline short so you can share with procurement and NetOps.

Recommendation summary (short):
- Default: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) per primary region for the Redwood inference service. Rationale: endpoint-level policies, per-service audit logs, least-privilege cross-account model, predictable perf for RPC workloads.
- Fallback for on-prem: S2S VPN tunnels for legacy DCs that cannot host interface endpoints; secure with MTLS and monitor.
- Use VPC Peering only for tightly-scoped low-latency pilots where both sides are in the same cloud account or under strict network governance.

Pilot scope & timeline (2–3 week pilot):
Week 0–1: Agreement & access
- Sign SOW (attached draft). Provide test AWS account IDs + desired CIDR ranges.
- Approve endpoint subnet + SG window and list of IPs for allowlist.

Week 1–2: PrivateLink pilot
- Redwood provisions interface endpoint service + NLB in our service account; EdgeBank creates interface endpoints in their VPC(s).
- Validate latency with synthetic tests and real sample traffic (aim: <50ms for simple requests).
- Configure endpoint policies, private DNS mapping, flow logs to your audit S3, and cert rotation plan.

Week 2–3: Optional S2S stitching & cutover plan
- Build S2S tunnels for legacy DCs; traffic steering rules configured for services that must traverse on-prem.
- Rollout canary traffic & failover routing.

Operational checklist (high level):
- Endpoint subnets: dedicated /27 for interface endpoints (isolate with NACLs).
- SGs: restrict to Redwood NLB CIDRs + management addresses.
- Certs: mTLS enforced between customer and Redwood; Automate rotation (90-day recommended).
- Observability: synthetic probes, per-endpoint latency histograms, flow logs pushed to audit S3, CloudWatch/Datadog hooks.

Attachments included: SOW-EdgeBank-draft.docx, privatelink-checklist.xlsx. HubSpot deal link for procurement: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/EB-2027-042

If youd like, I can schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff Thursday. Thanks — well keep the pilot intentionally small so NetOps can validate before wider rollouts.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
